Hi Vincent,

I'm running some Actigraph GT3X+ files with GGIR and getting this error with one of the files I'm running, any thoughts on what it means?

Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, count2:((count2 - 1) + nrow(NWav)), col_mli, value = c(3,  :
  subscript out of bounds

I've attached the "processing status updates" that are printed to the console, and I'm seeing "[1] "variabel metashort extended"" line which I haven't seen before, so maybe that'll help narrow down the issue.

If you want to see a copy of the file just let me know and I'll send you a link to it.

Thanks!
Suni

messages.subject: GT3X+: Large ENMO values with ActiLife Vector Magnitude calculation equal to zero?
messages.subject_clean: GT3X+: Large ENMO values with ActiLife Vector Magnitude calculation equal to zero?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

My group is attempting to do a comparison of daily MVPA estimates with different accelerometer locations and processing methods. One of the methods we're using is GGIR, and to do the comparison we're extracting minute-level MVPA classifications from GGIR and matching them to the counts from the the ActiLife software. When I do this I'm seeing that about 17% of minutes marked as MVPA by GGIR for the hip accelerometer have a zero vector magnitude from ActiLife. I know that the processing techniques are different but when we look at the matching wrist data I see that GGIR is also classifying those minutes as "not MVPA". I don't know why this would happen and wanted to get your opinion if this would be just a difference in algorithms or a bug? I'm attaching a quick screen grab to show you the inconsistency I'm seeing but if you need/want the full raw acceleration file or any other material please let me know and I can send that to you. It seems like this happens with a couple of participants for all their data (that pushes their MVPA minutes to several hundred for the day) and with others I'm only seeing it on a few days.

Thanks in advance for your help.
~ Suni

For your info:
The GT3X+ was set to record at 30 Hz and participants wore a wrist device and hip device for approximately 7 days.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GT3X+: Large ENMO values with ActiLife Vector Magnitude calculation equal to zero?
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GT3X+: Large ENMO values with ActiLife Vector Magnitude calculation equal to zero?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Suni,

Good that you are investigating this. Do I understand it correctly
that you are comparing Actigraph monitor data processed by Actilife
against the same data processed by package GGIR? If not, then you
would first have to investigate whether timestamps are compatible
between accelerometers and whether accelerometers were actually worn
by the same.

Are you applying the auto-calibration method? If not, then try to do
it or alternatively repeat your analyses with metric BFEN, which
should behave more similar to Actigraph counts than metric ENMO.
Metric ENMO is sensitive to poor sensor calibration.

I have no reason to believe that wrist acceleration is always higher
than hip acceleration. It probably depends on the activity type a
person was doing.

The fact that the counts are zero for the Actilife software might
indicate that the signals were of such a nature that the Actilife
software decided that it was not representing true body movement and
filtered it out. This is of course speculation, so you would have to
look at the raw data to get a better understanding of what might have
happened.

I hope this helps,

Best wishes,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

Yes, I'm comparing Actigraph monitor data processed by ActiLife against the same data processed by the package GGIR. One of our engineering students has also developed a machine learning package for activity recognition and we'll present that data too (although not a formal  comparison because it classifies walking and not MVPA).

I did apply the auto-calibration method, and my PI wants to keep the analysis to the best method published in your studies and I think that was ENMO, but maybe if I have some time I'll checkout the BFEN for my own edification.

I'll look into the possibility that the signal for those time intervals was filtered out by ActiLife.

Thanks for your input.
~ Suni

messages.body_plain:
Hi Suni,

In my 2013 PLoSONE paper I concluded that there is no obvious best
metric and that the best choice of metric may actually depend on the
kinematic conditions under which it is used.

To move forward with other studies I had to make a pragmatic decision
on what metric to use. I used the following motivations:
- Metric ENMO will not cause lengthy discussions about what filter
setting or moving average window size to use because metric ENMO does
not have a filter and it does not use a moving average filter.
- Continuing to use the same metric at least creates consistency
between the studies
- We proved in 2013 that metric ENMO at least has some value for
explaining variance in daily energy expenditure, so there is evidence
that this metric is not that bad.
- We did not find convincing evidence that any other metrics
structurally outperform metric ENMO. The metric HFEN+ which I
presented in the paper might with hindsight be a better choice, but
this metric is rather difficult to describe which causes the risk for
errors in replication by third parties.

Only a hand full of studies have been written that looked at the issue
of gravity separation in accelerometer data. This makes it difficult
to make any hard conclusions.

Thanks,

Vincent
